display.title: Eliyahu HaNavi's Cup
display.summary_short: A Yiddish Pesach story told by a grandmother: a poor mother refuses to sell her family's precious Kos shel Eliyahu, and an old man's two dollars that keep coming back bring the family a beautiful Seder.
display.summary_long: Told in Yiddish by a grandmother to her grandchildren. A once-wealthy family has lost everything, and Pesach is coming. The father wants to sell the one treasure left, a diamond-studded cup of Eliyahu HaNavi handed down in the mother's family for generations, but she refuses: Hashem will help. In despair he leaves for the shul. On a cold, rainy day, two days before Pesach, the children invite in a soaked old man. He asks to join their Seder and gives the mother two dollars for matzah and wine. Each time she spends them, two dollars are back in her pocket, so she buys food, clothes, curtains, a new kapote and hat for her husband, and fixes the roof and stove. The father comes home to a shining house and his wife explains. That night the father falls asleep just before the door is opened for Eliyahu, who comes in, tells the children of all the Sedarim he visits, and promises to return. The next night the same happens: Eliyahu says the father may not see him because he wanted to sell the cup, but the mother's home will be blessed until Moshiach comes.
display.lesson: Treasure what is holy and trust Hashem even when things look hopeless; Eliyahu HaNavi comes to every Jewish child's Seder.

advisories.note: A family loses everything and has nothing for Pesach; the father storms out in despair.
